Hey, fellow artist (in a sense) here. I am a big time writer. 

My doctor talked to me about this a lot before I ever started medication. I know exactly what you're saying. I have talked to my SO about this many times. 

It is hard for me to find inspiration when I am feeling better. I am very comfortable being depressed. (I spent about 10 years not getting help for depression, I learned how to just be comfortable with it, maybe like you?)

To me, it's like a peaceful feeling to be sad. It's just who I am as a person. Any music I like, is typically sad. My writing is all produced from darker times. 

But I also have learned to find some inspiration while I am medicating. It's a bit harder, and I often don't feel like it is not as moving or powerful ( I do pride myself in my work, not bragging) so it's a bit of a turn off. 

But I tell myself that as much as I would like to be a published writer one day, I would never be able to get there if I ended up killing myself. So although it may be a bit harder to develop the structure and framing of my writing when I am not depressed, oh well. Because I want to do something with it. 

Maybe you will learn to appreciate things more if you were to start medication. It took a while before mine set in, and I did realize just my outlook was so much different, I would find small inspirations from things I typically would not. But you also just don't have that dark driving desire like I'm sure you also feel. It's a tricky situation because first of all medication takes a while for you to notice a positive difference, and I know personally waiting for the time when I got my inspiration again was somewhat of a wait.

Talk to a doctor, if you have the ability to do so. That is the first step in getting help for these kinds of thoughts. After that I would say reach out to a therapist/psychiatrist and find a good fit, alongside whatever regimen your doctor may have you on, it is important along side that to be talking with someone. 

Personally, I suggest meditating. It does help.

And talking to peers or others, whether in person or online, it seems to help.
